items.t: Nvidia shares drop after hours amid reports of meeting over CEO Jensen Huang’s future
items.d: Shares of Nvidia dropped quickly in after-hours trading amid multiple reports that the company’s board would meet Wednesday night to discuss CEO Jensen Huang’s future and amid a New York Times report that he had a relationship with an executive who reported to him.
items.fullText: BREAKING NEWS Nov. 11, 2026, 11:51 PM UTC Business News Business News Nvidia shares drop after hours amid reports of meeting over CEO Jensen Huang’s future The New York Times reported that Huang had a relationship with an Nvidia executive, following reports that he’d had a relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Nvidia chips are the cornerstone of the artificial intelligence boom, powering all of the top developers, from OpenAI to Anthropic. Jean Chung / Bloomberg via Getty Share Add NBC News to Google By Rob Wile and Steve Kopack Shares of Nvidia dropped quickly in after-hours trading amid multiple reports that the company’s board would meet Wednesday night to discuss CEO Jensen Huang’s future and amid a New York Times report that he had a relationship with an executive who reported to him. Shares fell as much as 8%. The Times report , which cited five people who worked at Nvidia, followed reports in recent days that Huang had been involved in a relationship with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. NBC News has not confirmed the Times report or reports that the company’s board was meeting Wednesday night. The Wall Street Journal first reported the board’s plans, citing people familiar with the matter. Huang wrote in a note to employees Sunday that he had been “unfaithful to his wife,” though did not specify details. NBC News reported that officials believe the first woman, Alice Huang , was a Chinese intelligence operative. China has denied the allegations. items.t: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
items.d: The affair could have ramifications for national security as the U.S. and China race to develop the most advanced AI infrastructure.
items.fullText: Nvidia co-founder CEO Jensen Huang has never been as flashy or controversy-prone as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. Now, the 63-year-old industry kingpin has admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in an affair that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and potentially impact national security. United States officials believe that Huang’s likely romantic interest, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.) Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company, had reportedly purchased $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, the Times has reported. The story took a sudden new turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of health care, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up. Separately, the Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust Huang , and Nvidia’s shares fell in after-hours trading. The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. items.t: Nvidia Working With Outside Firm to Identify CEO Candidates
items.d: Nvidia Corp.’s board has been working with an outside firm to identify potential replacements for Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang following reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman who is reportedly suspected of spying for China, a person familiar with the situation said.

items.t: Nvidia’s stock drops as board reportedly preps to oust CEO Jensen Huang
items.d: As soon as Wednesday evening, Nvidia's board could decide to remove its founder and CEO of 33 years.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 3:28 PM PST · November 11, 2026 Image Credits: Tomohiro Ohsumi / Getty Images Amanda Silberling Nvidia’s stock drops as board reportedly preps to oust CEO Jensen Huang Nvidia is reportedly planning to oust its co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang, who has led the company for the last 33 years, the Wall Street Journal reports . Sources told the newspaper that the Nvidia board is meeting as soon as Wednesday to determine Huang’s future at the company. On Sunday, Huang admitted to having an extramarital affair with a woman purported by U.S. intelligence to be a Chinese spy. On Wednesday evening, the New York Times reported that Huang also had an affair with an executive who reports to him. Nvidia has become one of the most valuable companies in the world as it designs the chips that power the AI boom, but in the midst of Huang’s ongoing scandal , Nvidia stock fell about 8% in after hours trading on Wednesday. The stock is down about 11% in the past five days. Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said . The company also has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan. Jensen Huang accused of having another affair — with an Nvidia exec
items.d: Jensen Huang, who has come under fire for admitting to an affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese intelligence agent, has been accused of having a separate affair with an Nvidia subordinate.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 3:17 PM PST · November 11, 2026 Image Credits: Benjamin Fanjoy / Getty Images Lucas Ropek Jensen Huang accused of having another affair — with an Nvidia exec Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is already under investigation after having admitted to having an affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy . Now the New York Times is reporting that Huang is also suspected of having another extramarital affair, with a direct report of his at the company — Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare. Powell, like Huang, is married, the outlet says. The Times says it was told of the alleged affair by five employees at the company. The sources said that Huang and Powell were captured on video “being affectionate at a San Jose, Calif., hotel” during a conference earlier this year. Like many companies, Nvidia has rules discouraging superiors from having relationships with employees in subordinate roles, the Times notes. TechCrunch reached out to Nvidia for comment. The company’s board has initiated an investigation into Huang’s publicly admitted affair. Additionally, two House Republicans said Wednesday that Congress is gearing up to subpoena Huang over the spy allegations if he doesn’t voluntarily respond to their summons to a closed-door briefing. Late Wednesday, after the reports of the second affair were published, the Wall Street Journal reported that the Nvidia board was preparing to oust Huang, who co-founded the company in 1993. WSJ은 이날 사안에 정통한 복수의 소식통을 인용해, 엔비디아 이사회가 중국 스파이 혐의를 받는 여성과의 관계를 포함해 총 두 건의 혼외 관계를 맺은 황 CEO를 축출(oust)할 준비를 하고 있다고 전했다. WSJ 보도에 따르면 엔비디아 이사회는 빠르면 이날 중으로 회의를 열어 황 CEO의 최종 거취를 결정할 예정이다. WSJ은 이번 조치가 중국 스파이로 의심받는 여성과의 외도에 대한 회사 측의 내부 조사에 이은 것이라고 명시했다. 앞서 WSJ과 뉴욕타임스(NYT) 등 미 언론은 황 CEO가 미 정보당국이 중국 정보기관과 연계된 자산으로 의심하는 전직 메가스피드 임원 앨리스 황과 부적절한 관계를 맺어 이사회 조사를 받고 있다고 보도한 바 있다. 지난 주말 황 CEO가 해당 관계를 시인하고 이사회가 지난 8일 황 CEO에 대한 신임 입장을 밝히며 진화에 나섰으나, 이날 NYT가 황 CEO와 그의 직속 보고 라인인 킴벌리 파월 엔비디아 헬스케어 부문 부사장 간의 두 번째 혼외 관계를 추가로 폭로하면서 사태가 급변했다. 두 번째 불륜 보도 직후 나온 WSJ의 해임 준비 속보는, 안보 리스크가 불거진 첫 외도에 이어 사내 직속 부하 임원과의 추가 불륜까지 드러나자 이사회가 결국 해임 쪽으로 기류를 바꿨음을 시사한다. 황 CEO는 1993년 엔비디아를 공동 창업해 글로벌 AI 반도체 시장을 석권한 상징적 인물이다. 그러나 엔비디아가 미 증권거래위원회(SEC)에 제출한 2026년 공시 자료 및 외신 분석에 따르면, 황 CEO의 지분율은 3.58% 수준이며 1주 1의결권 구조상 차등의결권(슈퍼보팅)을 보유하고 있지 않아 이사회가 결의할 경우 법적으로 해임이 가능하다. 한편, 이날 정규 장에서 2.87% 상승했던 엔비디아 주가는 WSJ의 황 CEO 해임 준비 보도 직후 시간 외 거래에서 8% 이상 급락하며 크게 출렁이고 있다. 이형두 기자 dudu@etnews.com

items.t: Congress to call Jensen Huang in to answer for alleged Chinese spy affair
items.d: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has until the end of the day Wednesday to answer a call from House Republicans for a closed-door briefing on his affair with alleged Chinese spy.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 11:22 AM PST · November 11, 2026 Image Credits: Jose Sarmento Matos/Bloomberg / Getty Images Rebecca Bellan Congress to call Jensen Huang in to answer for alleged Chinese spy affair Congress is gearing up to subpoena Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to answer their questions about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy , Bloomberg reports , citing two House Republicans. The report comes a week after House Republicans Brian Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford sent a letter to Huang asking him to appear before their committees for a joint, closed-door briefing in regards to his relations with Alice Huang, the Megaspeed executive and suspected Chinese spy. House China committee Chairman Moolenaar said Wednesday on Fox Business that Huang has until the end of the day to respond to the request. If he doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be subpoenaed, said Moolenaar. Mast, who chairs the House Foreign Affairs Committee, on Wednesday said his committee is preparing a subpoena for Huang to send if he doesn’t respond. Nvidia did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment. items.t: Is Jensen Huang’s bad behavior more commonplace than it seems?
items.d: “There are a lot of senior people in the industry that know this is happening, and are effectively condoning it,” an investment intel consultant said.
items.fullText: The AI industry is still reeling from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s honeypot scandal, but some in the industry see it as an issue that’s much larger than one man. The Chinese government has been active in economic espionage for decades, and with semiconductors at the center of the AI boom, there’s intense pressure to infiltrate any company involved. At the same time, many of the executives getting rich off that boom have made themselves easy targets. As CEO of investment intel firm Heron Intelligence, Nate Singer has a unique view into the problem. His firm works on corporate due diligence: Essentially, making sure companies know the relevant dirt before making a major acquisition or executive hire. And while the Nvidia case is particularly severe, Singer says there are lots of similar cases in the semiconductor industry that have stayed under the radar. “We’ve got former employees talking about behavior at senior executive levels,” Singer told TechCrunch, saying executives are “really crossing lines that should not be crossed.” In a widely circulated LinkedIn post , Singer detailed one case in which a CEO’s wife made an unexpected board room appearance, “screaming about her husband and another company exec flying around in the corporate jet with a couple young ladies (who also turned out to be state-sponsored actors).” It’s an alarming story, but an unfortunately common one. Singer says he’s seen at least three reports of similar cases, and suspects many more have gone unreported. “There’s a lot more than this one woman,” Singer said. “They are embedded in these companies.” Semiconductor companies are already big targets for international trade secret theft. There have been dozens of prosecutions for similar cases in recent years, including a case involving the fabrication powerhouse TSMC in 2007.
